correctness.rationale: The center is forced by the uniqueness of the planar center of area and dihedral symmetry. The directional halfplane problem is solved analytically: a radial integral gives F'(theta)=1/2(rho(theta+pi/3)^2-rho(theta)^2), and on a dihedral fundamental interval the two radial values lie on the same generating circle, where their scalar ray parameters differ by sin(theta)/sqrt(3). This proves the global minimum exactly. The minimum area is then an elementary circular-segment integral. The packaged checker independently reconstructs the three-disk intersection and replays the formulas.

value.rationale: The Reuleaux triangle is the canonical nonsymmetric body of constant width and a standard extremal test object for symmetry measures. Winternitz measure is a classical invariant and simultaneously the maximum halfspace depth of the uniform distribution, so an exact value supplies a reusable benchmark in convex geometry and depth statistics. The theorem also identifies the exact worst directions and separates the invariant from the distinct metric-diameter asymmetry used in constant-width literature.
